pointers.sentence: A built-in field is a subclass of `Field` that overrides a few of its parts: its `widget`, messages and validators, `widget_attrs` for the widget's HTML attributes, and `to_python`, which makes the value ([A form field: the base class](fields.md)) (`django/forms/fields.py:Field.__init__`).

A required field, `NullBooleanField` aside, refuses an empty value with the code `"required"`; the last column is what one that is not required makes of `""` or `None` (`django/forms/fields.py:Field.validate`).

`FloatField` and `DecimalField` are subclasses of `IntegerField` and share its limits: `max_value`, `min_value` and `step_size` become validators, the step counted from the minimum or from 0 ([Validators: `django/core/validators.py`](validators.md)), and `IntegerField.widget_attrs` writes them on a `NumberInput` as `"min"`, `"max"` and `"step"` (`django/forms/fields.py:IntegerField.widget_attrs`).

`FloatField` and `DecimalField` are subclasses of `IntegerField` and share its limits: `max_value`, `min_value` and `step_size` become validators, the step counted from the minimum or from 0 ([Validators: `django/core/validators.py`](validators.md)), and `IntegerField.widget_attrs` writes them on a `NumberInput` as `"min"`, `"max"` and `"step"` (`django/forms/fields.py:IntegerField.widget_attrs`).

For a `DecimalField` with `decimal_places` and no `step_size`, `DecimalField.widget_attrs` makes the step one unit of the last decimal place, as `str` writes it, in lower case: `"0.01"` for the draught, and `"1e-7"` for seven places, an exponent that, the comment says, keeps a small value from being parsed as 0 (ticket 20765) (`django/forms/fields.py:DecimalField.widget_attrs`).
`float` and `decimal.Decimal` accept `"inf"` and `"NaN"`, and `FloatField.validate` and `DecimalField.validate` refuse a value that is not finite (`django/forms/fields.py:DecimalField.validate`).

Its value is written in the locale's format and read with `sanitize_separators` ([Locale formats: `get_format` and the format modules](../i18n/formats.md#reading-a-value-back)) (`django/forms/fields.py:IntegerField.__init__`).

`DateField`, `TimeField` and `DateTimeField` hand a string to `BaseTemporalField.to_python`, which strips it and tries the field's `input_formats` one by one with `datetime.datetime.strptime`, refusing it as `"invalid"` when none fits (`django/forms/fields.py:BaseTemporalField.to_python`).
Then come the `DATETIME_INPUT_FORMATS` and after them the `DATE_INPUT_FORMATS`, so a date alone is read as its midnight (`django/forms/fields.py:DateTimeField.to_python`).

Under `USE_TZ`, `from_current_timezone` makes a naive result aware in the current time zone, and refuses a time that the zone skips or repeats as `"ambiguous_timezone"`; a result with an offset keeps it (`django/forms/utils.py:from_current_timezone`).
`DateTimeField.prepare_value` goes the other way, so that an input shows an aware value in the current zone's time (`django/forms/utils.py:to_current_timezone`).

Beside a file already there, for a field that is not required, `ClearableFileInput` draws a box to clear it, and reads the pair as one value: the upload, `False` for the box alone, or the marker `FILE_INPUT_CONTRADICTION` for both ([Widgets: `Widget` and its subclasses](widgets.md)) (`django/forms/widgets.py:ClearableFileInput.value_from_datadict`).
`FileField.clean` is given the initial value too, by `FileField._clean_bound_field` (`django/forms/fields.py:FileField.clean`).

When a model form fills its instance, a model's file field keeps its file for `None` and is emptied by `False` ([File fields](../instance/files.md)) (`django/db/models/fields/files.py:FileField.save_form_data`).
`FileField.has_changed` counts anything but `None` from the widget as a change, unless the field is disabled (`django/forms/fields.py:FileField.bound_data`).
`ImageField.to_python` adds Pillow, imported when an image is cleaned (`django/forms/fields.py:ImageField.to_python`).
Its validator `validate_image_file_extension` refuses an extension Pillow does not know, and a file input with no `"accept"` gets `"image/*"` (`django/forms/fields.py:ImageField.widget_attrs`).
`BooleanField.validate` refuses a false value for a required field: a required `BooleanField` is a box that must be ticked (`django/forms/fields.py:BooleanField.validate`).

`NullBooleanField` reads `"True"`, `"true"` and `"1"` as `True`, their opposites as `False` and anything else as `None`, and its `validate` does nothing, so being required refuses nothing (`django/forms/fields.py:NullBooleanField.to_python`).
`MultiValueField` makes one value of several inputs: it is given a list of fields, and a `MultiWidget` reads one string for each (`django/forms/fields.py:MultiValueField.clean`).

`SplitDateTimeField` is a `DateField` and a `TimeField` drawn by a `SplitDateTimeWidget`; its `compress` joins them and passes the result through `from_current_timezone` (`django/forms/fields.py:SplitDateTimeField.compress`).

`ComboField` is the reverse, one value that must pass several fields: after its own required check and validators, its `clean` hands the value to each field's `clean` in turn (`django/forms/fields.py:ComboField.clean`).

`URLField.to_python` strips the value and, if it finds no scheme, puts the field's `assume_scheme` in front, by default `"https"`: `"harbour.example/berths"` becomes `"https://harbour.example/berths"` (`django/forms/fields.py:URLField.to_python`).
`JSONField` is a `CharField` drawn as a `Textarea`, whose `to_python` decodes with `json.loads` (`django/forms/fields.py:JSONField.to_python`).
